history.summary: The ISKCON temple in Chandigarh - Hare Krishna Dham - stands on Dakshin Marg in Sector 36B, Chandigarh 160036 (some listings say Sector 36 - verify). It belongs to the International Society for Krishna Consciousness (Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition) and serves as the movement's centre for the Tricity: daily Mangala arati, Srimad-Bhagavatam lectures, Sunday programmes with aarti/kirtan and prasadam, book stalls, a cafeteria and devotional merchandise. Visitors describe it as a well-maintained, serene temple with a large main hall; Sunday evening aarti is popular. Exact founding year and deity installation details were not found in published sources (verify).

town_description: Chandigarh, Le Corbusier's planned city and joint capital of Punjab and Haryana (a Union Territory), is organized in numbered sectors. Sector 36 is a central residential/commercial sector on Dakshin Marg. The ISKCON temple sits on the main road and is easily reached within the city's grid.

travel.road: Hare Krishna Dham, Dakshin Marg, Sector 36B; on the main road, reachable by city bus, taxi or auto (verify sector numbering 36 vs 36B).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather. Janmashtami is the grandest celebration; Sunday evenings are popular for aarti and kirtan.
